references.text: Describes the Feast of Weeks (Shavuot), where one must count fifty days and present a new grain offering to the Lord, the same feast mentioned in Numbers 28:26.
Mentions the Feast of Weeks with the firstfruits of the wheat harvest, corresponding to the bikurim day in Numbers 28:26.
Detailed description of the Feast of Weeks with instructions about the new grain offering and that it should be a holy assembly where no work is to be done.
Command to celebrate the Feast of Weeks seven weeks after the grain harvest begins, with voluntary offerings to the Lord.
Pentecost (Greek: Pentekoste) is the Greek term for the Feast of Weeks/Shavuot, the day when the Holy Spirit was poured out on the disciples.
Paul wished to be in Jerusalem by Pentecost, showing that this feast was still celebrated in the early church.
Paul mentions that he intends to stay in Ephesus until Pentecost, demonstrating the continued significance of the feast.
